claim: Hashed reduced-alphabet sketches (sourmash FracMinHash, protein/dayhoff/hp, k 7-13, scaled 10-1000) can stand in for DIAMOND to search a whole gene catalog for a protein
rule: Step 1: whole OM-RGC v2 sketched in <= 1536 CPU-hours (two days of a 32-CPU node) at some scaled. Step 3: some setting finds >= 80% of DIAMOND's pairs at E < 1e-5 with shuffled copies hitting < 1% as many genes as real queries
result: Step 1 run 2: whole OM-RGC v2 sketched in 34-77 CPU-h per scaled value (fits 1536). Step 3 (27 settings incl. scaled 10, 2026-10-20): no setting passes. DIAMOND: 31865 real-query pairs at E<1e-5, 0 for shuffled copies. hp k7/k10 at scaled 10/100 and hp k13 at scaled 10 find 91-100% of DIAMOND's pairs but shuffled copies hit 0.98-1.04x as many genes as real queries; lowest shuffled rate protein k13 scaled 100 (1.7%) finds 5 of 31865. Run 1 'dead at step 1' was a sourmash .zip-writer artefact.
what_was_not_done: Step 4 (kmerseek layer) not run: step 3 did not pass. BHF gather run against the 1% gene sample only.
